paper.title: The coverage of influenza vaccination and predictors of influenza non-vaccination in Danish cancer patients: A nationwide register-based cohort study
paper.code_data_availability: Data availability statement: 'The authors do not have permission to share data.' Ethics: …

registers.role: sample frame; treatment/predictor (cancer type, cancer stage, date of diagnosis, years since diagnosis)
outcome (influenza vaccinations administered by general practitioners, registered for reimbursement); predictor (previous influenza vaccination)

registers.years: up to ten years before each influenza season through 2017/2018
registers.role: outcome (vaccination during hospitalization); predictor (systemic anti-cancer therapy; comorbidity for free-of-charge eligibility); previous influenza vaccination
variables_mentioned: systemic anti-cancer therapy (chemotherapy, non-immunosuppressive therapy, no systemic therapy)

registers.years: up to two years before each influenza season through 2017/2018
registers.role: outcome (vaccination prescriptions redeemed at Danish pharmacies); predictor (medication for diabetes or chronic lung disease for free-of-charge eligibility); previous influenza vaccination
linkage (unique personal identification number); predictors (sex, place of birth, cohabitation, mortality during the influenza vaccination season); residence and emigration
variables_mentioned: mortality during the influenza vaccination season (no death, died October, died November, died December onwards)

registers.role: predictor (highest achieved education level: low, medium, high)
variables_mentioned: highest achieved education level (low, medium, high)

registers.role: predictor (early retirement, used in the definition of eligibility for free-of-charge influenza vaccination)

registers.name_in_paper: the Danish clinical quality databases (The Danish Clinical Quality Program - National Clinical Registries)
registers.role: supplementary predictors in a subpopulation (smoking, body mass index, performance status, alcohol consumption)

linkages: All registers are linked at the individual level using the unique personal identification number assigned to all Danish citizens at birth or upon immigration
Cancer patients (DCR) linked to influenza vaccination records in DNHSR, DNPR and DNPrR per influenza vaccination season

Patients linked to the Danish clinical quality databases (prostate, colorectal, gynecological, acute leukemia, lung, chronic myeloid neoplasia and lymphoma registries) for the supplementary health and lifestyle analysis

sample.universe: All Danish citizens aged >=18 years with an incident cancer diagnosis in one of 23 pre-specified cancer groups registered in the Danish Cancer Registry from October 1, 2002 to October 1, 2017
sample.unit_of_observation: patient-influenza vaccination season (an individual influenza vaccination season experienced by a cancer patient)
selection_rules: Patients aged >=18 years with an incident cancer diagnosis between October 1 2002 and October 1 2017: N=438,239 (Figure 1)
Exclude patients with an incident cancer diagnosis not included in the pre-specified cancer groups (n=69,250), leaving N=368,989
Exclude diagnoses of non-invasive, benign, or pre-cancerous conditions (Appendix A2)
Exclude patients with two different diagnoses on the date of the incident primary cancer diagnosis (n=748)
Exclude patients without recorded residence in Denmark on the date of the incident primary cancer diagnosis (n=2052)
Exclude patients with missing information on cohabitation or place of birth in the season under investigation or the prior season (n=34,877)
Exclude patients with missing information on highest reached education (n=11,817)
Exclude patients only eligible for inclusion in one season but not diagnosed on or prior to October 1 in that season (n=3367)
Exclude patients not eligible for inclusion in any influenza vaccination season
Patients are eligible for up to five influenza vaccination seasons after their incident cancer diagnosis; seasons run from 2007/2008 to 2017/2018
For each season, inclusion is conditioned on diagnosis on or before October 1 of that season
A new primary cancer or emigration before or during an influenza vaccination season excludes the patient from that season onwards
Death before a season excludes the patient from that season onwards, but patients who die during a season under observation are retained in that season
sample.period: Influenza vaccination seasons 2007/2008 to 2017/2018; incident cancer diagnoses October 1, 2002 to October 1, 2017
sample.n_observations: 840,876 individual influenza vaccination seasons (351,200 in patients aged <65 years, 489,676 in patients aged >=65 years)
sample.n_individuals: 269,863 patients (117,207 aged <65 years and 152,656 aged >=65 years on October 1 of their first observed influenza season)

construction_notes: Influenza vaccination seasons are defined as the free-of-charge vaccination period: October-December for seasons 2007/2008-2013/2014 and October-February for seasons 2014/2015-2017/2018
Influenza vaccination status is assessed at the end of each influenza vaccination season

Seasons start in 2007/2008, which corresponds to the introduction of free-of-charge influenza vaccination for individuals with acquired immunodeficiency; free-of-charge vaccination for citizens aged >=65 years has been in place since 2002

Systemic anti-cancer therapy is assessed from the DNPR in the period from three months before October 1 until the end of the vaccination season, categorised as chemotherapy, non-immunosuppressive therapy, or no systemic therapy

Eligibility for free-of-charge influenza vaccination for other reasons than age, cancer type or chemotherapy combines early retirement at any time point, DNPR registrations of diabetes, cardiovascular disease, immunodeficiency, chronic kidney failure, chronic liver failure or chronic lung disease within ten years prior to the start of the current season, and medication for diabetes or chronic lung disease administered two years prior to the start of the current season
Previous influenza vaccination is a binary indicator built from DNHSR, DNPR and DNPrR for the season preceding the season under observation
All analyses are conducted separately for patients aged <65 and >=65 years, following the Danish age criterion for free-of-charge influenza vaccination
Standard errors are made robust to repeated seasons per patient by clustering within the personal identification number
The study follows the STROBE reporting guidelines

claims.statement: Influenza vaccination coverage over the 11 influenza seasons 2007/2008-2017/2018 combined was 51 % among Danish cancer patients aged >=65 years, compared with 14 % among cancer patients aged <65 years.

treatment.label: Aged >=65 years at October 1 of the influenza vaccination season (reference: aged <65 years)

register_source.value: Danish National Patient Registry (DNPR) for systemic anti-cancer therapy; Danish Cancer Registry (DCR) for cancer type; Danish Civil Registration System for age

definition.value: Age group at October 1 of the influenza vaccination season, >=65 years versus <65 years, the age criterion for free-of-charge influenza vaccination in Denmark.

timing.value: Defined per influenza vaccination season; chemotherapy is assessed from three months before October 1 until the end of the season, age at October 1 of the season, cancer type at the incident diagnosis.

outcome.label: Influenza vaccination coverage (%)

register_source.value: Danish National Health Service Register (DNHSR), Danish National Patient Registry (DNPR) and Danish National Prescription Registry (DNPrR)

definition.value: Unadjusted proportion (%) of observed influenza vaccination seasons in which the patient has a registered influenza vaccination, presented as an overall estimate for all seasons combined and separately by season, for groups defined by each combination of cancer type (solid tumour, haematological cancer, lymphoma) and chemotherapy receipt.

timing.value: End of each influenza vaccination season; overall figure pools the 11 seasons 2007/2008-2017/2018.

units.value: percent of observed influenza vaccination seasons with a registered influenza vaccination

magnitude.interpretation: The authors note this is below the 75 % target recommended for persons aged >=65 years and for persons with chronic diseases.

estimand.target_population: all Danish cancer patients observed in influenza vaccination seasons 2007/2008-2017/2018
estimand.time_horizon: all influenza vaccination seasons 2007/2008-2017/2018 analysed combined; each patient contributes up to five influenza vaccination seasons after the incident cancer diagnosis

population.description: all Danish cancer patients observed in influenza vaccination seasons 2007/2008-2017/2018
population.ages: >=18 years at cancer diagnosis; compared at <65 vs >=65 years
population.period: influenza vaccination seasons 2007/2008 to 2017/2018; incident cancer diagnoses October 1, 2002 to October 1, 2017
population.selection: All Danish citizens aged >=18 years with an incident diagnosis in one of 23 pre-specified cancer groups in the Danish Cancer Registry, observed in up to five influenza vaccination seasons after diagnosis; patients with two different diagnoses on the incident date, without recorded residence in Denmark at diagnosis, with missing cohabitation or place of birth in the current or previous season, or with missing highest reached education were excluded; a new primary cancer, emigration or death before a season removed the patient from that season onwards.

identification.source_of_variation: No exogenous variation: unadjusted coverage proportions compared across register-defined groups of cancer type, chemotherapy receipt and age in a nationwide cohort.

key_assumptions.assumption: Influenza vaccinations given by general practitioners, during hospitalisation and redeemed at pharmacies are captured in the DNHSR, DNPR and DNPrR, so that an absent record means the patient was not vaccinated.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The authors state that influenza vaccination codes have not been validated, that the MMR vaccine is underreported due to administrative errors, and that they expect the vaccinated proportion to be underestimated.

key_assumptions.assumption: Exclusion of patients with missing information on education, cohabitation or place of birth in the current or previous season is non-differential with respect to vaccination.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The authors state that this may introduce non-differential selection, that the proportion of missing data was small, and that place of birth did not have a considerable impact on vaccination.

implies_edges.from: sample inclusion: complete register information on education, cohabitation and place of birth
implies_edges.to: Influenza vaccination coverage (%)

key_assumptions.assumption: Repeated influenza seasons contributed by the same patient are not independent; robust variance with clustering on the personal identification number is used to relax the independence assumption.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Stated in the statistical analysis section as the reason for using Poisson regression with robust variance and clustering within ID.

key_assumptions.assumption: The adjusted prevalence ratios are interpreted as predictors of (associations with) influenza non-vaccination after mutual adjustment for all included variables, not as causal effects; no exogenous variation is invoked.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper throughout speaks of 'predictors' and of variables being 'associated with' non-vaccination, and offers no identification argument beyond mutual adjustment.

threats_discussed: Influenza vaccination codes in the Danish national registries have not been validated; underreporting is expected, so the vaccinated proportion is probably underestimated

Non-reimbursed vaccinations (e.g. offered by workplaces) are not captured, which could cause differential misclassification for patients with the longest time since diagnosis or lower-stage cancer and bias away from the null
Patients with missing information on education, cohabitation or place of birth were excluded, which may introduce non-differential selection
Chemotherapy combined with additional therapies could not be classified, so the proportion of treatment-induced immunocompromised patients is likely underestimated
Eligibility for free-of-charge vaccination for other reasons was built from diagnosis and medication codes and may not include everyone deemed eligible by their general practitioner
robustness_checks: Sensitivity analysis restricted to influenza seasons beginning <=1 year after the incident cancer diagnosis (Supplementary Fig. 2)
Sensitivity analysis excluding the 2007/2008 season to ensure validity of 'Previous influenza vaccination' (Supplementary Fig. 3)
Supplementary analysis restricted to immunocompromised patients: solid tumour patients receiving chemotherapy, haematological cancer patients, and lymphoma patients (Figs. 4 and Supplementary Fig. 4)
Supplementary analysis of patients aged >=65 years split into 65-74, 75-79, 80-84 and >=85 years (Supplementary Fig. 5)
Supplementary analysis in the subpopulation registered in the Danish clinical quality databases with health and lifestyle factors (Supplementary Figs. 6-12)
unresolved_confounders: Differential misclassification of vaccination status if underreporting occurs in those with the longest time since diagnosis or in those with lower-stage cancer who may have returned to work, which would bias away from the null
Underestimation of the proportion of patients who are immunocompromised because of treatment, and of the proportion eligible for free-of-charge vaccination for other reasons

estimator.value: unadjusted proportion (influenza vaccination coverage, %), no regression model

estimation.specification: Coverage presented as an overall estimate for all seasons combined and separately by season, for all included patients combined and for groups defined by each combination of cancer type (solid tumour, haematological cancer, lymphoma) and chemotherapy receipt, within age strata.
